video_title: Will The Blazers Really Leave Portland? The Truth Behind Tom Dundon | KOC x Adam Gold

quotes.speaker: Adam Gold
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dundon's two distinct approaches to team ownership
quotes.excerpt: There are two Tom Dundons. There is the owner of the team, Tom Dundon.
quotes.quote: There are two Tom Dundons. There is the owner of the team, Tom Dundon. We are talking about the team on the court for the Hurricanes and the team on the ice, and everything that impacts that team, Tom has been absolutely incredible at. He made every decision correctly. They had a plan when they came in, they stuck to that plan, and it culminated in winning a Stanley Cup last year. The truth is they have been a legitimate Stanley Cup contender now for like four years.

quotes.speaker: Adam Gold
quotes.summary_phrase: The other side of Tom Dundon's business-first ownership style
quotes.excerpt: That is the Tom Dundon that became a billionaire on the backs of less fortunate people.
quotes.quote: Then there is the other Tom Dundon that I feel like the Blazers and the NBA establishment are dealing with. And that is not the good Tom Dundon. That is the Tom Dundon that became a billionaire on the backs of less fortunate people, that doesn't have much empathy towards others. He is very much 'what is the bottom line?' That is big business Tom Dundon. He has been incredibly successful doing that.

quotes.speaker: Adam Gold
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dundon's controversial decision to eliminate Chuck Kaiton's radio broadcast
quotes.excerpt: One of the first things he did was eliminate the radio broadcast of a hockey Hall of Famer.
quotes.quote: One of the first things he did was eliminate the radio broadcast of a hockey Hall of Famer. Chuck Kaiton is in the broadcasting wing of the Hockey Hall of Fame, still on that committee. He had spent 39 years with the Whalers and Hurricanes franchise, called every game that they had done, including the Stanley Cup in 2006, was part of the team in 2009 when they went to the conference finals, and his last season was the 17-18 season, the year Tom Dundon assumed ownership midstream, and then they dumped the broadcasting.

quotes.speaker: Adam Gold
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dundon's lack of value for non-winning business operations
quotes.excerpt: Tom Dundon doesn't see value in things that do not directly add to winning.
quotes.quote: Tom Dundon doesn't see value in things that do not directly add to winning. So, simulcasting TV, radio in for the Blazers, that was always going to happen. He is going to go as cheap as he can on the things that do not impact winning, and everything that you have seen him do with Portland is with that mindset, whether it is the two-way contract players that are in the playoffs or team employees not getting what they had been getting before.

quotes.speaker: Adam Gold
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dundon's original intent to move the Carolina Hurricanes
quotes.excerpt: When he bought the Hurricanes, his intent was to move them.
quotes.quote: In fact, my understanding is that when he bought the Hurricanes, his intent was to move them because he didn't think it would work out. He saw a depressed asset, which is what he does. So when he bought the Hurricanes, I think he was like, 'I don't think we are going to make it here,' and he knew he could move them to Houston possibly or Austin. He doesn't realize how hard it is to relocate a franchise in the NHL, especially one where the commissioner values the market.

quotes.speaker: Adam Gold
quotes.summary_phrase: The problem with owners asking taxpayers to fund arena renovations
quotes.excerpt: I hate asking the public to basically finance your playground.
quotes.quote: I hate asking the public who are going to pay tickets, pay for parking, and pay for concessions. I hate asking the public to basically finance your playground. I don't think it's right. We have too many things that government needs to do, needs to provide for, let alone do your building. But what I think and what the reality is are two different things, because that's the way things are done in professional sports. They feel like they've got leverage, they can move the team, and I think he would love to move the team if he can't get everything he wants from Portland.

quotes.speaker: Adam Gold
quotes.summary_phrase: NHL versus NBA roster building and star power requirements
quotes.excerpt: In the NHL, you can win without superstar caliber players.
quotes.quote: In the NHL, you can win without superstar caliber players. The Hurricanes are proof of that. In the NBA, man, you got to have stars. And in the NBA, you can throw your draft picks away to bring a star in. We see it routinely. The Knicks traded four first-round picks for Mikal Bridges. You can't do that. They don't do that in hockey. And he will value those draft picks. They are more likely to sell players for draft picks than trade a bunch of draft picks away for star players.

quotes.speaker: Adam Gold
quotes.summary_phrase: The failed trade of Jake Guentzel to Carolina
quotes.excerpt: Jake Guentzel came from Pittsburgh to Carolina and then ultimately signed with Tampa in the off-season.
quotes.quote: Before he made the trade, you may not know Jake Guentzel came from Pittsburgh to Carolina and then ultimately signed with Tampa in the off-season. That was a deal that Carolina screwed up. He wanted to stay with the Hurricanes, but they lowballed him an offer enough to where he goes, 'Well, let me just look around,' and he got a better deal from Tampa. I asked him if he was more likely to do it again, he goes, 'No, I'll never do it again.'

quotes.speaker: Adam Gold
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dundon's refusal to make moves that only marginally increase winning
quotes.excerpt: I'm not going to do anything that only increases my chances of winning by one or two percent.
quotes.quote: He said, 'I'm not going to do anything that only increases my chances of winning by one or two percent. That doesn't work for me.' That's the way he thinks. We add a player, does it increase our chances of winning? They've got a formula, and he said, 'For one or two percent, never going to do it again, unless it's something that we have to have,' which they have done in the past, but that isn't a trade deadline move to me.

quotes.speaker: Adam Gold
quotes.summary_phrase: Rod Brind'Amour's status as a franchise legend and coach
quotes.excerpt: Rod Brind'Amour, first of all, franchise legend. He was already an established great player in Philadelphia.
quotes.quote: Rod Brind'Amour, first of all, franchise legend. He was already an established great player in Philadelphia at the time Jim Rutherford made the trade to bring him to Carolina back in 2000, and then decided to stay, won a cup, and now as the coach, won another cup. But they're going to name streets for parts of highways for Rod Brind'Amour when it's all done. There will be statues, and a lot of kids will be named Rod in Raleigh.
